newsitem.title: USA: USDA offers more aid to Plains flood victims.
newsitem.headline: USDA offers more aid to Plains flood victims.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday that the agency would offer additional assistance to flood victims in the Dakotas and Minnesota, including emergency farm loans and help for livestock producers.
"USDA will show maximum flexibility and will commit maximum resources -- from food assistance, to farm aid, to personnel and vehicles," Glickman said in a statement.

USDA will extend the Foundation Livestock Relief program for 15 days and make cost-share assistance retroactive to February 25. A further 15-day extension would also be considered, he said. The program provides cost-share assistance to livestock producers in counties that have lost 40 percent or more of normal feed production.
The USDA is allowing emergency grazing on Conservation Reserve Program lands, beginning May 1, Glickman said. The agency will make a decision about CRP land for haying sometime after June 1.

About 90 percent of the acreage in the affected areas is covered by federal crop insurance. "The preliminary estimate, assuming losses as bad as those in 1995, is about $160 million in prevented planting alone," the USDA said.

Some $46 million is currently available in the USDA's Farm Service Agency emergency farm loan fund, he said. Farmers in counties declared disaster areas can apply for low-interest loans from the program.
The Clinton Administration has asked for an extra $60 million in disaster legislation to supplement the emergency farm loan fund.

Glickman said USDA would send special teams of loan specialists to the three affected states to process loan applications as quickly as possible. And the agency is also working with the Federal Emergency Management Agency on how to remove the carcasses of animals that died in the flooding.
Glickman said he also directed Farm Service Agency directors to use discretionary authority to mitigate foreclosure proceedings.
